scene.dock: The crew stands in {place}, crates stacked high and one cold lamp swinging overhead. A corridor leads inward and a vent gapes in the wall.
Dust hangs in {place}. The hauler is somewhere beyond, and the only ways in are the corridor and a narrow vent.
The crew arrives at {place} with the shift bell long gone. Nobody is here, and every door is either too quiet or too loud.
scene.corridor: The crew edges along {place}, pipes ticking on both sides. Something metal scrapes ahead.
Inside {place} it is narrow and badly lit. A draught carries the smell of hot oil from the far end.
Footsteps echo through {place}. The crew can push on or look for another way around.
scene.vent: The crew crouches in {place}, the grille cold under their hands. A faint glow shows below.
Inside {place} it is tight and smells of burnt dust. Far below, a screen flickers in an empty room.
The crew slides into {place}. The only choices are to drop down or to turn back.
scene.ambush: Two scrappers step out of the shadows at {place}, tools raised and in no mood to talk.
The crew reaches {place} and finds it blocked. Scrappers with rivet guns spread out to cut off the way back.
A shout rings out at {place}. Scrappers charge in from both sides.
scene.airlock: The crew reaches {place}. A heavy lock stands between them and the hauler, and a light on the far side blinks red.
Inside {place} the air hums with idle pressure. A warden stands on the other side of the glass, watching.
The crew steps into {place}. The inner door is sealed, and the control panel waits for a steady hand.
scene.control: The crew breathes out in {place}. Every screen shows the hauler bay, and the warden is moving toward it.
Inside {place} it is quiet apart from the hum of the machines. The doors can be sealed, or the hauler can be flown out right now.
Lights wake up across {place} as the crew arrives. There is not much time.
scene.warden-fight: The warden turns in {place} and raises a pulse pistol. A scrapper lurches in beside them.
Inside {place} boots ring on the deck. The warden blocks the ramp and the scrapper covers the flank.
In {place} there is nowhere left to hide. The warden fires first.
scene.escape: The hauler lifts free and the dock falls away behind it. The crew is out, and the night is theirs.
Engines roar and the doors blur past. The crew has made it out alive, and the frontier opens ahead.
The hauler clears the last gate. Nobody is chasing, and the crew can finally laugh.
scene.lost: The crew goes down in the dark and the dock falls silent. The frontier keeps its secrets this time.
Alarms fade as the last light goes out. The hauler stays where it is, and so does the crew.
It ends here, quietly. Another crew will have to try the dock tomorrow.
scene.out-of-time: The shift bell rings and the doors lock for the night. The crew has run out of time.
Dawn shift arrives and the dock fills with workers. The crew slips out before anyone looks closely.
Time runs out and the lamps flick off one by one. The crew will try again another night.
combat.start: Weapons come up and the room goes still.
Somebody fires first, and then everyone does.
The standoff breaks. It is a fight now.
check.success: {character} gets the {skill} just right, and it holds.
check.failure: {character} tries {skill}, but it does not come together.
The {skill} slips from {character}'s hands, and it costs them.
{character} misses with {skill} and has to think again.
check.complication: Something shifts at the worst moment as {character} reaches for {skill}.
{character} hears a sharp crack while using {skill}, and not from the plan.
A small thing goes wrong around {character} while they try {skill}.
wound.stunned: {target} staggers and shakes their head, stunned.
The blow rings through {target}, who is stunned.
wound.wounded: {target} takes a solid hit and is wounded.
wound.severely-wounded: {target} cries out. That one was severe.
Another hit on {target}, who is now severely wounded.
wound.incapacitated: {target} cannot go on and is out of the fight.
{target} falls and does not get up. Incapacitated.
wound.mortally-wounded: {target} is mortally wounded and goes down hard.
That blow nearly finishes {target}, who is mortally wounded.
wound.dead: The fight ends for {target}, for good.
